description: A medium to large Amanita with an olive to dark brown cap 5-10 cm across, covered in small white warts. The gills are white, the stem has a ring, and the base is swollen with a collar-like rim. The spore print is white.
habitat: Grows from soil, partnered with the roots of conifers and hardwoods.
lookalikes: Amanita rubescens (Blusher, edible): bruises pinkish-red where cut; this species does not
Other pale Amanita species, including deadly ones: check the base and the spore print, not the cap colour
safety_notes: POISONOUS AND PSYCHOACTIVE: contains ibotenic acid and muscimol. Effects are unpredictable and can include nausea, confusion, delirium, seizures and coma. Listed for identification and safety only. Never eat a wild mushroom on an app's word. If anyone has eaten this species, call poison control or emergency services.
